summary: Pre-FOMC nerves showed up as a two-sided reversal. NQ sold from its opening range into a 27,603.25 low, then V-recovered 356 points to close 27,959.75 and flip its ATR stop back to LONG, though still red on the day at -0.89%. ES did the same, closing +0.19% and back above its 7,430.45 stop. The catch: both indices sit right at their AVWAPs, so the flips are repairs, not confirmed trends. Gold went the other way. Yesterday's lone haven long rolled over, lost 4,071.10, and flipped SHORT at -1.23%. Crude kept bleeding, down another -3.41% to 79.12 after Monday's -9.43%, and stays deeply short. This is positioning drift into a Wednesday Fed decision, and the tape says both sides can get run before it resolves.
psychology: Today rewarded patience and punished the knife-catchers on both ends. If you shorted the opening-range break down in NQ, you were right for two hours and then watched a 356-point reversal stop you out. If you tried to pick the exact low, you sat through more heat than the setup was worth. The lesson holds into a Fed day: on event-driven reversals, let the market prove direction with a close, not a wick. A stop reclaimed late in the day is information, not an invitation to chase size at 4pm. Size for the decision, not the last hour.

event.crossAsset: Equities flipped long (NQ and ES) while gold flipped short (-1.23%, losing its haven bid) and crude extended lower (-3.41%). A risk-on tilt in equities against weakness in havens and energy.
